# Thurbox

> Thurbox is a multi-session TUI for coding agents — Claude Code and Codex,
> through Fleet's harness profiles — running inside persistent tmux panes. Every
> session is a Fleet Task: Fleet starts it in the repository you pick and keeps
> it running, so sessions survive crashes and restarts. It is written in Rust,
> open source under the MIT license, and runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows
> (plus remote hosts over SSH). Fleet's `fleet` command line drives the same
> sessions for scripting; `thurbox-cli` covers the interface's own files.
>
> Installing: run
> `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Thurbeen/thurbox/main/scripts/install.sh | sh`
> on Linux/macOS, or
> `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Thurbeen/thurbox/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex`
> on Windows, or `nix profile install github:Thurbeen/thurbox` with Nix, then
> run `thurbox`. That is the whole setup — config, themes and the interface
> itself are seeded on first launch.
>
> Its defining feature is that the interface is fully customizable: no UI is
> compiled into the binary. thurbox boots a Rust kernel that reads a
> directory of Lua files and draws whatever it finds, so every pane — the
> session list included — is a file the user can move, turn off, delete,
> rewrite, or install from someone else, with no recompile and no restart. The
> arrangement (`ui/layout.lua`), hosts (`hosts.toml`), themes, keybindings and
> settings are all data files. Because the interface is
> plain text in a directory, the usual way to change it is to ask a coding
> session for the change in English — the directory ships an `AGENTS.md` that
> tells whichever CLI is running how the interface is put together, so "add my
> project logs within a dedicated pane on the right in the thurbox UI" works
> from a session opened there. The same holds for orchestration:
> a session's agent can run `fleet`, so "using fleet, start refactor sessions
> for this repo, one per crate" spins up a fleet without a script.

## Docs

- [Documentation hub](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/index.html): entry point to all Thurbox documentation.
- [Tutorial](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/tutorial.html): onboarding walkthrough with screenshots — adding a repository to the picker, creating a first session in a repository, the everyday keybindings, and the equivalent fleet commands.
- [FAQ](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/faq.html): short answers to the most common questions (what it is, how it differs, install, platforms, license).
- [Features](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/features.html): the customizable interface, sessions, agent definitions, git worktrees, sessions on other Fleet hosts, automations, global search, headless CLI.
- [Agents](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/agents.html): the agents are Fleet's harness profiles (claude, codex); thurbox keeps no agent registry and reads no agents.toml.
- [Comparison](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/comparison.html): how Thurbox compares to Conductor, Claude Squad, Cursor, and other parallel coding-agent tools.
- [Installation](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/installation.html): install via curl, Homebrew, AUR, Nix/NixOS, winget, Chocolatey, or from source; prerequisites; running it; how to pin a specific version.
- [Orchestration](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/orchestration.html): Fleet (https://github.com/Thurbeen/fleet), an orchestrator that runs one Thurbox session per Task — install, its Task loop, and the Fleet Lens pane (https://github.com/Thurbeen/thurbox-fleetlens) that browses it from Thurbox — plus asking an agent to spin up sessions with thurbox-cli, and the Thurbox primitives Fleet is built on.
- [Configuration](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/configuration.html): every config file and knob — hosts.toml, settings.toml, themes, keybindings, and the Fleet thurbox uses.
- [The Interface](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/interface.html): every pane is an editable Lua plugin — how to move, disable, replace or write one, how a plugin reacts to events and puts actions in the Ctrl+P command palette, how to have a coding agent do it for you, what the kernel refuses a plugin, and the panes you install (thurbox-code-review, thurbox-info-panel).
- [Architecture](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/architecture.html): the Lua-on-Rust plugin kernel and its five rules, module isolation, the tmux session backend, and the decisions behind them.
- [Removing old hook entries](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/extensions.html): Thurbox v3 installs nothing into an agent's config; how to delete by hand the status hooks, status files and skills Thurbox v2 wrote into each agent's config.
- [Recipes](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/recipes.html): worked patterns for orchestrating multi-session, multi-repo workflows.

## Optional

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Thurbeen/thurbox): source, README, and releases.
- [Keybindings](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/keybindings.html): the Vim-inspired keyboard reference.
